statement: In 5 of 5 analysed books framed by bedtime or sleep the last spread is quieter than the book's average (0-2 of 5 against an average of 2.1-3.1); in non-bedtime books this holds for 8 of 17, and many end on a joyful payoff at or above the average. None of the 21 books has a celebration after the story: they close with a picture, a vignette or credits.

scope.population: contemporary open-licence picture books: Book Dash, StoryWeaver/Pratham Books, African Storybook; 2014-2026

analyst_note: 2026-10-21: answers the reader agent's question q_what_is_on_the_last_spread_of_the_analys. Two publishers among the 5. Intensity is on the 0-5 research scale; on the engine's 0-3 scale the last bedtime pages are 0-1 (Zuko about 1). Emotion intensity measured 100% re-read agreement (24 pages).

magicpaper.current: After the last page StoryReaderView stops narration and goes straight to StoryEndingLeaf: Ragi waving, 'Masal bitti!', reading counts and a 400 ms celebration, the same in every mode.
magicpaper.suggested: In bedtime mode only: let the last story page stand alone as a quiet moment (no auto-advance, narration ends softly), and make the ending leaf calm: no celebration animation and no reading counts on that screen; keep today's ending for adventure and learning.
